Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

style noun

a way of doing something, especially of speaking or writing

also style of writing, style of speaking, in the style of, architectural style

classical

Cic. Brut. 165: Antōnī genus dīcendī
Cic. Brut. 302
M-O s.v. style (architectural): architectūrae genus

genus, generis n.

noun, third declension

a kind; a style

genus dīcendī, a style of speaking.

Other words

  • stilus, stilī m. — the pen; a manner of writing

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 150: stilus exercitātus (Lewis & Short)

    Properly the writing stylus, then writing practice and the manner of writing.

Examples

  • Antōnī genus dīcendī multō aptius jūdiciīs quam contiōnibus

    Antonius’ style of speaking was much better suited to the courts than to public meetingsCic. Brut. 165

  • attuleratque minimē vulgāre genus dīcendī

    and he had brought a style of speaking that was far from commonCic. Brut. 302

See also style, kind, approach.
